note: Merged/ready real issue documenting hook-manager coexistence; today's A4 limited_scope criterion false-positives on its own "coexistence"/config-surface prose (known lexical-gate boundary gap).
title: docs(customization): cover hook-manager coexistence when the worktree guard claims core.hooksPath
body:
## Background

Parent roadmap: #1937

The B1 worktree guard is activated by claiming `core.hooksPath` for
`.githooks`, per the guidance roadmap #1156 shipped through #1158.
`core.hooksPath` is shared, non-worktree-scoped repository config.

Husky v9 ships `"prepare": "husky"` in `package.json`, which every
`pnpm install` triggers, and it resets `core.hooksPath` to `.husky/_`
unconditionally. So in a repository that already uses Husky,
the guard is correctly wired, then silently un-wired by the next
dependency install in any worktree — and `idd-doctor`'s #1157
enabled-but-inert warning correctly reappears each time, moments after
the operator re-wired it.

Field-reported from `kurone-kito/web-toybox` and independently from
`kurone-kito/builder-config`. This is not the "never wired" case
#1157/#1158 address; it is "wired, then reset by unrelated tooling",
which their guidance does not cover. The combination is not exotic for
the profile it affects: `docs/onboarding/policy-decisions.md`
auto-proposes `package-manager` for any repository with a supported
lockfile, and a hook manager is common in exactly those repositories.

Roadmap #1156 recorded, as an explicit non-goal, that it would not ship
an auto-wiring install/prepare hook, "left out unless a maintainer
requests it". **This issue does not build that mechanism and does not
reopen that non-goal.** It adds the coexistence guidance that was never
part of it — which is why the "never wired" documentation shipped while
this failure mode stayed undocumented.

## Proposed change

Extend the worktree-guard activation guidance with a hook-manager
coexistence section covering the case where `core.hooksPath` is already
owned by another tool:

- State that `core.hooksPath` is repository-wide, not worktree-scoped,
  so one install in any worktree changes it for all of them.
- State that a hook manager whose own install step sets `core.hooksPath`
  will reclaim it on every dependency install, and that the recurring
  `idd-doctor` enabled-but-inert warning is the expected symptom rather
  than a detection defect.
- Give the chaining recipe as the recommended resolution: keep the
  existing manager's hook path and have each of its hooks `exec` the
  corresponding `.githooks/*` script, so neither tool has to win
  ownership of `core.hooksPath`.
- Note the fully-replace alternative in one sentence, without
  prescribing it, since it removes the other tool from the repository.
- Add a portability caveat for the chaining recipe: a lifecycle script
  run through pnpm's `shellEmulator` supports simple chaining
  (`&&`, `||`, `;`, `exit`) but not POSIX control-flow keywords, so a
  fail-closed guard written as `if ... then ... fi` fails with
  `command not found: if`. Show the emulator-safe form instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- The worktree-guard activation guidance carries a hook-manager
  coexistence section with all five points above.
- The chaining recipe is shown as a concrete snippet, not prose alone.
- The `shellEmulator` caveat shows an emulator-safe fail-closed form
  that still lets a genuine failure propagate.
- The section states explicitly that no automatic wiring mechanism is
  provided, and that manual activation stays the contract.
- The `docs/customization.md` worktree-guard row links the new section.
- `docs/customization.md` syncs in `exact` mode from
  `idd-template/docs/customization.md`, so the template source is
  edited and `node scripts/sync-docs.mjs --apply` regenerates the
  repository copy; `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` reports no
  drift.
- `node scripts/audit-code-span-wrap.mjs` passes.
- `pnpm run lint:minimum` passes.

## Candidate files

- `idd-template/docs/customization.md`
- `docs/customization.md`
- `idd-template/docs/onboarding/policy-decisions.md`
